title: Accelerating a health-record rollout can outrun user readiness and operational proof
source_unit: GAO-26-109393 testimony summarizing GAO follow-up reports on VA Electronic Health Record Modernization
geography: United States Department of Veterans Affairs; VA health-care facilities and planned EHR deployments, 2017–2031 planning horizon

denominator.unit: GAO recommendations made across five prior VA EHR-related reports

recommendation_status.value: 4 implemented; 14 not fully addressed, including 10 not implemented and 4 partially implemented priority recommendations
recommendation_status.unit: GAO recommendation status as of August 2026

deployment_history.value: initial deployment in 2020, four additional sites in 2022, pause after user feedback, planned restart at four Michigan facilities and nine additional 2026 sites

cost_schedule.value: VA delivered a notional schedule but not an updated cost estimate or detailed schedule documentation sufficient for leading-practice assessment

user_readiness.value: users reported dissatisfaction and VA had not validated that the system satisfied user needs in the operational environment

observations.method: GAO testimony summarized five prior GAO reports from June 2020 through March 2025 and followed up with VA on recommendation implementation through August 2026; the underlying work addressed cost estimates, schedules, data management, user satisfaction, trouble tickets, change management, and operational testing.
observations.uncertainty: This testimony is a synthesis of prior reports and recommendation follow-up, not a new representative survey of all veterans or clinicians. Recommendation status is not the same as system performance, clinical safety, or patient outcomes. The planned deployment count is a schedule target, not completed implementation. User dissatisfaction and system issues are reported from prior work and are not a prevalence estimate for every site.
observations.subgroup: VA patients, clinicians, end users, initial deployment facilities, and planned deployment sites; the record does not provide a linked patient-clinician-site panel.
observations.counterinterpretation: Only four of 18 recommendations were fully implemented, but partial implementation can still improve some operations. A deployment pause can be a corrective action rather than simple failure. A missing cost estimate or independent operational assessment is a control gap, not proof that the system is unsafe or that every user experiences poor performance.

related_sources.claim: Official GAO testimony PDF provides the recommendation status, deployment history, cost/schedule gap, user feedback, and operational-assessment boundary.

boundary: This record adds a rollout-to-usability mechanism: system deployment and acceleration can coexist with unresolved cost, schedule, user adoption, operational testing, and patient-safety controls. It does not establish patient harm, clinical effectiveness, veteran satisfaction prevalence, or the success or failure of the planned 2031 rollout.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: Official GAO landing page and testimony PDF; VA system logs, patient records, and site-level performance data are not retained.
